title: Lease-based node fencing for reversible overlay rollout
creator: Liam Patel
description:
Problem: Existing data-plane rollouts for Private (VPC) deployments rely on draining and replacing nodes or performing immutable swaps. These approaches either cause transient connection drops or require expensive full-node image swaps that are hard to rollback within the same maintenance window. We need a safer upgrade approach that allows a fast rollback path without disrupting session affinity and without heavyweight node reprovisioning.

Proposal summary: Implement a lease-based node fencing mechanism paired with reversible overlay image rollouts that let us apply a layered overlay on top of the running runtime (via container image overlay or overlayfs) and route traffic to upgraded processes only after they signal healthy and hold a short-lived lease. If the rollout shows regressions, revoke leases and atomically unmount/revert overlays to restore the prior runtime state. Integrate this into our Terraform/IaC pipeline via preflight hooks and health-check gating to ensure the control plane can orchestrate rollouts across VPC tenants with zero-downtime guarantees.

Why different: Instead of replacing nodes or full-swap images, we rely on a lease token that represents traffic ownership for a node slice and reversible file-layer overlays so the rollback is immediate and does not require re-creating kernels, warming caches, or waiting for provider replacement. This approach reduces latency spikes during rollouts and shortens rollback mean time to recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Can deploy overlay to a single runtime node and acquire a lease before traffic is routed
Health-checks (synthetic and real) must pass for the upgraded overlay before additional leases are granted
Rollback path reverts overlay and releases leases within 15s with no in-flight request failures above baseline SLOs
Terraform module exposes preflight check, lease TTL, and reversible-overlay toggle and has automated plan/apply validation
End-to-end tests in staging that simulate KV cache mismatch and verify graceful rollback without service-level error spike
design_notes: Lease semantics: a short-lived (30-120s) lease TTL with automatic renewal; control plane revokes lease to stop routing to overlayed process

Overlay strategy: use overlayfs (or container image layer) to mount a delta overlay that contains binary patches, config diffs, and per-node local libraries; must be mountable/unmountable without restarting primary process when possible
Health gating: dual-path health-checks - (1) local process probe for readiness, (2) end-to-end synthetic request replay that validates model outputs for a representative prompt set
Terraform integration: add a module output hook that registers a rollout job with the control plane and performs 'terraform apply' then triggers the lease acquisition sequence via provider hook
Observability: emit events for lease-granted, lease-renewed, lease-revoked, overlay-mounted, overlay-unmounted. Add trace spans to the Console rollout timeline
Edge cases: node with sticky sessions must not be demoted until in-flight requests drain or are retried; implement fast-path token handoff for session rebinds
